chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad, both from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman ibn Dawud, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from al-Zuhri who said: I heard Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) saying:
'The verses of the Quran are treasures; so every time a vault is opened, it is befitting for you to look at what is in it.'

key_terms.آيَاتُ الْقُرْآنِ: The verses of the Quran — divine speech revealed to the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW)
key_terms.خَزَائِنُ: Treasuries/vaults — plural of khizanah, here a metaphor for the boundless wisdom contained in each verse
key_terms.يَنْبَغِي: It is befitting/proper — an expression of strong recommendation, just short of obligation

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Zayn al-Abidin say about the depth of Quranic verses?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin (AS), the fourth Imam, uses a powerful metaphor to describe the inexhaustible depth of Quranic verses — each verse is like a locked treasury full of knowledge and wisdom. The teaching encourages believers to approach each verse with curiosity and attentiveness, recognizing that each recitation or reflection may yield new insights. This hadith reflects the Shia emphasis on the multidimensional, layered nature of the Quran, whose meanings continue to unfold for those who engage with it deeply.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali Bin Muhammad, altogether from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Suleyman Bin Dawood, from Hafs Bin Giyas, from Al Zuhry who said, 
‘I heard Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> saying:
‘The Verse of the Quran are a treasure, so every time you open the vault, it is befitting for you that you look at what is in it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Ali ibn Muhammad all from al- Qasim ibn Muhammad from Sulayman ibn Dawud from Hafs ibn Ghiyath from al-Zuhri who has said the following: “I heard Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) saying, ‘
Verses of the Holy Quran are treasures, whenever a treasure is opened you should look into it.”’
